module.title: House, Rooms & Furniture: There is & There are
module.objective: Describe rooms, household furniture, and layout using 'there is' and 'there are' with prepositions of place.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Exploring Homes, Rooms & Furniture
subModules.grammarFocus: There is & There are (affirmative, negative, and question forms)
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Rooms in a house, common furniture, and household items

content.summary: Welcome to your Reading Mission! In this lesson, you will read a short, fun passage about a person describing their new home. You will learn how to understand descriptions of rooms and furniture using 'There is' for one thing and 'There are' for more than one thing. By the end, you will feel confident reading about houses and identifying what is in each room. Let's explore a new home together!

linguisticTarget.grammar: There is + singular noun (e.g., There is a lamp on the table.) and There are + plural noun (e.g., There are two chairs in the kitchen.). Negative forms: There isn't / There aren't. Question forms: Is there...? / Are there...?
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Rooms (kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom, dining room, garden) and furniture (sofa, table, chair, wardrobe, fridge, lamp, bookshelf, curtain, mirror, rug)
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the passage first to understand the main idea (What is the text about?). Then scan for specific details — look for 'There is' and 'There are' to find out what objects are in each room.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short A1 passage describing rooms and furniture in a house.
Identify key details about what items are in each room using 'There is' and 'There are'.
Recognize the difference between singular and plural nouns after 'There is' and 'There are'.
Practice scanning a text to find specific information about a home.
Build confidence reading everyday descriptions of living spaces in English.

contextWarmup.prompt: You are visiting a friend's new apartment. You walk into the living room. Which sentence correctly describes what you see?
options: There is a big sofa and there are two cushions on it.
There is a big sofa and there is two cushions on it.
There are a big sofa and there is two cushions on it.
contextWarmup.explanation: Great job! 'There is a big sofa' is correct because 'sofa' is one thing (singular). 'There are two cushions' is correct because 'two cushions' is more than one thing (plural). Always check: one thing = 'There is', more than one = 'There are'.

rules: Use 'There is' (or the contraction 'There's') before a singular noun: There is a bed in the room. / There's a lamp on the desk.
Use 'There are' before a plural noun: There are four chairs around the table. There are some books on the shelf.
For negative sentences, add 'not': There isn't a garden. / There aren't any pictures on the wall.
For questions, switch the order: Is there a bathroom upstairs? / Are there any windows in the kitchen?
Use 'a' or 'an' with singular nouns after 'There is': There is a mirror. Use 'some' or a number with plural nouns after 'There are': There are some plants. / There are three bedrooms.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Common Beginner Pitfall: Mixing Up Singular and Plural
commonTrap.explanation: Many beginners use 'There is' with plural nouns or 'There are' with singular nouns. Before you choose, always count the noun! If it is ONE thing, use 'There is'. If it is TWO or MORE things, use 'There are'. This is the most important rule to remember.
commonTrap.wrong: There is three windows in the bedroom.
commonTrap.correct: There are three windows in the bedroom.

sections.title: Reading Passage: Welcome to My New Home!

content.context: Maya just moved into a new house. She writes a message to her friend, Lina, to describe her new home. Read her message and find out what is in each room.
content.text:
Hi Lina! I am so happy! I have a new house. Let me tell you about it.

Downstairs, there is a big living room. There is a blue sofa and there are two small chairs. There is also a soft rug on the floor. There are white curtains on the windows. It looks very nice!

Next to the living room, there is the kitchen. There is a new fridge and there is a wooden table. There are four chairs around the table. There isn't a dishwasher, but that is okay.

Upstairs, there are two bedrooms. In my bedroom, there is a comfortable bed and there is a large wardrobe. There is a small lamp on the bedside table. There is also a bookshelf with some books.

There is one bathroom upstairs. There is a mirror on the wall, but there aren't any plants yet. I want to buy some plants soon!

Please come and visit me. You will love it!

highlights.note: Used before a singular noun — one thing (e.g., a big living room, a new fridge).
Used before a plural noun — two or more things (e.g., two small chairs, four chairs).
Negative form for singular — means 'there is not' (e.g., there isn't a dishwasher).
Negative form for plural — means 'there are not' (e.g., there aren't any plants).
On the lower floor of a house.
On the upper floor of a house.
A small carpet that covers part of the floor.
A piece of furniture with shelves for holding books.

gistQuestion.prompt: What is the main idea of Maya's message?
options: Maya describes the rooms and furniture in her new house.
Maya asks Lina to help her move to a new house.
Maya wants to sell her old furniture to Lina.
gistQuestion.explanation: Well done! The whole message is about Maya telling Lina what rooms and furniture are in her new house. She describes the living room, kitchen, bedrooms, and bathroom.

detailQuestions.prompt: What color is the sofa in the living room?
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage says 'There is a blue sofa.' So the sofa is blue. Great scanning!

detailQuestions.prompt: How many bedrooms are there upstairs?
detailQuestions.explanation: Maya writes 'there are two bedrooms' upstairs. The word 'two' tells us the number, and 'There are' is used because it is more than one.

detailQuestions.prompt: What does Maya NOT have in her kitchen?
detailQuestions.explanation: Maya says 'There isn't a dishwasher.' The negative form 'isn't' tells us she does not have one. She does have a fridge and a table.

detailQuestions.prompt: What does Maya want to buy for the bathroom?
detailQuestions.explanation: Maya writes 'there aren't any plants yet. I want to buy some plants soon!' So she wants to buy plants for the bathroom.

detailQuestions.prompt: Where is the bookshelf in Maya's house?
detailQuestions.explanation: In the paragraph about her bedroom, Maya says 'There is also a bookshelf with some books.' So the bookshelf is in her bedroom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is on the floor in the living room?
questions.explanation: Maya writes 'There is also a soft rug on the floor' when she describes the living room. A rug is a small carpet that covers part of the floor.

questions.question: Which sentence from the passage uses 'There are' correctly?
options: There are four chairs around the table.
There are a new fridge in the kitchen.
There are a comfortable bed in my bedroom.
questions.answer: There are four chairs around the table.
questions.explanation: 'There are four chairs' is correct because 'four chairs' is plural (more than one). The other options have singular nouns ('a fridge', 'a bed'), so they need 'There is'.

questions.question: Maya says 'There isn't a dishwasher.' What does this mean?
options: The kitchen does not have a dishwasher.
The kitchen has a new dishwasher.
Maya wants to remove the dishwasher.
questions.answer: The kitchen does not have a dishwasher.
questions.explanation: 'There isn't' means 'there is not.' It tells us that something does NOT exist in that place. So the kitchen does not have a dishwasher.

questions.question: How many chairs are there in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: The passage says 'There are four chairs around the table' in the kitchen section. Always scan for numbers to find specific details!

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence about Maya's bathroom.
options: There is a mirror on the wall.
There are many plants in the bathroom.
There is a bookshelf in the bathroom.
questions.answer: There is a mirror on the wall.
questions.explanation: Maya says 'There is a mirror on the wall, but there aren't any plants yet.' So there IS a mirror, but there are NO plants. The bookshelf is in the bedroom, not the bathroom.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct form: '_____ two bedrooms upstairs.'
questions.explanation: 'Two bedrooms' is plural (more than one), so we must use 'There are.' Remember: singular = 'There is', plural = 'There are'.

questions.question: What does Maya ask Lina to do at the end of the message?
options: Come and visit her new house.
Send her some money for plants.
questions.answer: Come and visit her new house.
questions.explanation: At the end, Maya writes 'Please come and visit me. You will love it!' She is inviting Lina to see her new home.

questions.question: Which room has a wardrobe?
questions.explanation: In the bedroom paragraph, Maya says 'there is a large wardrobe.' A wardrobe is a piece of furniture for keeping clothes, and it is commonly found in bedrooms.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Exploring a New House

content.summary: In this listening mission, you will hear a conversation between two friends. Rina is visiting Sarah's new house, and Sarah is showing her around. They talk about the rooms and furniture using 'There is' for one thing and 'There are' for more than one thing. Listen carefully for the names of rooms like 'living room', 'bedroom', and 'kitchen', and furniture words like 'sofa', 'bed', 'wardrobe', and 'table'. Pay attention to questions like 'Is there...?' and 'Are there...?' because these are used to ask about things in a house.
learningObjectives: Identify rooms in a house such as living room, bedroom, and kitchen when mentioned in spoken English.
Understand the difference between 'There is' (singular) and 'There are' (plural) in natural spoken dialogue.
Recognize common furniture vocabulary like sofa, bed, wardrobe, table, and TV in listening passages.
Understand yes/no questions with 'Is there...?' and 'Are there...?' and their short answers.

keyPhrases.phrase: There is a big TV on the wall.
keyPhrases.note: Use 'There is' (or 'There's') before a singular noun to say something exists in a place.
Use 'There are' before a plural noun (two or more items) to describe what exists.
This is a yes/no question form for singular nouns. The answer is 'Yes, there is' or 'No, there isn't'.
This is a yes/no question form for plural nouns. Use 'any' in questions. The answer is 'Yes, there are' or 'No, there aren't'.
Use 'How many + plural noun + are there?' to ask about the number of things in a place.
A friendly phrase used when you want to give someone a tour of a place like your house.

connectedSpeech.note: 'There is' contracts to 'There's' in fast natural speech. The 'i' sound in 'is' disappears completely.
'There are' can sound like 'there-er' in fast speech. The word 'are' becomes very short and blends with 'there'.
In fast speech, 'Is there a' links together and sounds like 'iz-ther-uh'. The three words blend into one smooth sound.
'Are there' links together in natural speech so it sounds like 'ar-ther'. The two words flow without a pause.
'Let me' contracts to 'lemme' in casual fast speech, and 'you' reduces to 'yuh'.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Describe Your House with There is & There are

content.summary: In this writing blueprint, you will learn how to describe rooms and furniture in a house. You will use 'There is' for one thing (singular) and 'There are' for two or more things (plural). You will also learn how to write negative sentences with 'There isn't' and 'There aren't', and how to ask questions with 'Is there...?' and 'Are there...?'. Follow the steps below to build clear sentences and short paragraphs about your home.

blueprintItems.title: Use 'There is' for One Thing
blueprintItems.formula: There is + a/an/one + singular noun + place.
blueprintItems.example: There is a lamp on the table.

blueprintItems.title: Use 'There are' for Two or More Things
blueprintItems.formula: There are + number/some + plural noun + place.
blueprintItems.example: There are two windows in the bedroom.

blueprintItems.title: Make Negative Sentences
blueprintItems.formula: There isn't + a/an + singular noun + place. / There aren't + any + plural noun + place.
blueprintItems.example: There isn't a garden behind the house. There aren't any pictures on the wall.

blueprintItems.title: Ask Questions About a Room
blueprintItems.formula: Is there + a/an + singular noun + place? / Are there + any + plural noun + place?
blueprintItems.example: Is there a mirror in the bathroom? Are there any bookshelves in the living room?

mechanicsRules.rule: Always start your sentence with a capital letter and end it with a period (.) or question mark (?).
mechanicsRules.badExample: there is a bed in my room
mechanicsRules.goodExample: There is a bed in my room.
mechanicsRules.why: Every English sentence must begin with a capital letter and end with correct punctuation. This makes your writing clear and correct.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'a' or 'an' before a singular noun after 'There is'. Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds.
mechanicsRules.badExample: There is sofa in the living room.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: There is a sofa in the living room.
mechanicsRules.why: Singular countable nouns need an article ('a' or 'an') after 'There is'. Without the article, the sentence is incomplete.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'any' in negative sentences and questions with plural nouns. Use 'some' in positive sentences with plural nouns.
mechanicsRules.badExample: There aren't some chairs in the kitchen.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: There aren't any chairs in the kitchen.
mechanicsRules.why: In negative sentences and questions, we change 'some' to 'any'. We use 'some' only in positive sentences.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not forget to add '-s' or '-es' to make a noun plural after 'There are'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: There are three bedroom in my house.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: There are three bedrooms in my house.
mechanicsRules.why: After 'There are', the noun must be plural. Add '-s' or '-es' to show more than one.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Describing Your House with There is & There are

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will learn how to describe rooms and furniture in a house using 'There is' for singular items and 'There are' for plural items. You will practise clear pronunciation of room names, furniture vocabulary, and the natural rhythm of 'There is' and 'There are' sentences. Pay attention to how native speakers link words together, for example 'There‿is‿a' sounds like 'Theriza' and 'There‿are' sounds like 'Therr-ar'. You will also practise rising intonation for yes/no questions like 'Is there a sofa?' and falling intonation for statements like 'There is a table in the kitchen.'
content.audioGuidance: When you say 'There is a sofa', connect the words smoothly: 'ther-IZ-uh SO-fuh'. Do not pause between 'there' and 'is'. For 'There are two chairs', say 'ther-AR too CHAIRZ'. In questions like 'Is there a bed?', your voice should go UP at the end. In statements like 'There are three books on the shelf', your voice should go DOWN at the end. Practise speaking slowly first, then try to speak at a natural speed.

pillars.name: Linked Speech
pillars.target: Smooth connection of 'There is' and 'There are'
pillars.explanation: In natural English, 'There is a' links together and sounds like 'Theriza'. 'There are' links to sound like 'Therrar'. Practise saying these as one smooth unit, not three separate words.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Stress on key content words (nouns and adjectives)
pillars.explanation: In the sentence 'There is a BIG SOfa in the LIving room', the important words BIG, SOfa, and LIving get more stress. The grammar words 'there', 'is', 'a', 'in', 'the' are said quickly and softly.

pillars.name: Intonation Patterns
pillars.target: Rising intonation for yes/no questions, falling for statements
pillars.explanation: When you ask 'Is there a TABLE? ↗', your voice rises at the end. When you answer 'Yes, there IS. ↘ There is a table in the KITCHEN. ↘', your voice falls at the end. This helps your listener know if you are asking or telling.

pillars.name: Clear Vowel Sounds
pillars.target: Accurate pronunciation of room and furniture vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Practise the vowel sounds in key words: 'kitchen' has a short /ɪ/ sound, 'bedroom' has a long /iː/ sound, 'sofa' has the /əʊ/ sound, and 'wardrobe' has the /ɔː/ sound. Clear vowels help people understand which room or furniture you mean.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Both 'bedroom' and 'bathroom' are compound nouns. The stress falls on the FIRST part: BEDroom and BATHroom. The second part 'room' is always unstressed.

The word 'table' has stress on the first syllable: TAble. The word 'comfortable' also has stress on the first syllable: COMfortable. Notice that 'comfortable' is often pronounced as three syllables in natural speech: COMF-ter-ble.
Both 'kitchen' and 'living room' have stress on the first syllable. KITchen and LIving room. In compound nouns for rooms, the stress is almost always on the first word or syllable.

The word 'furniture' has three syllables with stress on the first: FURniture. The word 'wardrobe' has two syllables with stress on the first: WARDrobe. Both follow the pattern of stressing the first syllable.

drills.targetText: There is a sofa in the living room.
drills.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈsəʊ.fə ɪn ðə ˈlɪv.ɪŋ ruːm/
drills.hint: Connect 'there is a' so it sounds like 'theriza'. Put stress on SOfa and LIving.

drills.targetText: There are two chairs and a table.
drills.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr tuː tʃeəz ənd ə ˈteɪ.bəl/
drills.hint: Say 'therrar' for 'there are'. Make sure 'chairs' ends with a clear /z/ sound, not /s/.

drills.targetText: Is there a bed in the bedroom?
drills.phonetic: /ɪz ðeər ə bed ɪn ðə ˈbed.ruːm/
drills.hint: Your voice should go UP at the end of this question: bed-ROOM? ↗ Start lower and rise on the last word.

drills.targetText: There is a big wardrobe next to the window.
drills.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə bɪɡ ˈwɔː.drəʊb nekst tə ðə ˈwɪn.dəʊ/
drills.focus: Stress on adjective and key nouns
drills.hint: Stress the important words: BIG WARDrobe and WINdow. Say 'next to' quickly as one unit: 'nekstuh'.

drills.targetText: Are there any books on the shelf?
drills.phonetic: /ɑːr ðeər ˈen.i bʊks ɒn ðə ʃelf/
drills.focus: The /ʃ/ sound in 'shelf' and rising intonation
drills.hint: The 'sh' in 'shelf' is a soft sound /ʃ/. Push your lips forward slightly. Remember to raise your voice at the end because this is a question.

drills.targetText: There are three rooms in my house.
drills.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr θriː ruːmz ɪn maɪ haʊs/
drills.hint: For 'three', put your tongue between your teeth for the /θ/ sound. For 'house', open your mouth wide for the /aʊ/ sound: ha-OWs.

roleplay.context: Mr. Khoirul is your English tutor. He is visiting your home for the first time. He asks you to describe the rooms and furniture in your house. Use 'There is' for one thing and 'There are' for two or more things. Try to speak clearly and use the vocabulary you have learned.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Today, let's talk about your house. How many rooms are there in your house?
turns.translation: Halo! Hari ini, mari kita bicara tentang rumahmu. Ada berapa ruangan di rumahmu?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There are five rooms in my house.
turns.translation: Ada lima ruangan di rumah saya.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's nice! Tell me about your living room. What furniture is there?
turns.translation: Bagus! Ceritakan tentang ruang tamumu. Perabotan apa yang ada di sana?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There is a big sofa and there are two chairs. There is also a TV on the wall.
turns.translation: Ada sebuah sofa besar dan ada dua kursi. Ada juga TV di dinding.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Wonderful! Now, describe your bedroom. Is there a wardrobe in your bedroom?
turns.translation: Luar biasa! Sekarang, deskripsikan kamar tidurmu. Apakah ada lemari pakaian di kamar tidurmu?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, there is. There is a wardrobe and a comfortable bed. There are some books on the table.
turns.translation: Ya, ada. Ada sebuah lemari pakaian dan tempat tidur yang nyaman. Ada beberapa buku di atas meja.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Excellent! Last question: Are there any plants in your house?
turns.translation: Bagus sekali! Pertanyaan terakhir: Apakah ada tanaman di rumahmu?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, there are. There are three plants in the living room.
turns.translation: Ya, ada. Ada tiga tanaman di ruang tamu.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Look at the three story points below. Tell a short story about your living room. Use 'There is' and 'There are' to describe what is in the room. Speak for about 30 seconds.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please describe your living room. Tell me what furniture and things are in it. Use 'There is' for one thing and 'There are' for more than one thing.
storyPoints: Talk about the size of your living room and one big piece of furniture (for example: a sofa or a TV).
Describe two or more smaller items in the room (for example: chairs, cushions, or pictures).
Mention something on the wall or near the window (for example: a clock, a painting, or curtains).
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a big sofa in my living room. There are two small chairs and a coffee table. There is a painting on the wall near the window.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə bɪɡ ˈsəʊ.fə ɪn maɪ ˈlɪv.ɪŋ ruːm. ðeər ɑːr tuː smɔːl tʃeəz ənd ə ˈkɒf.i ˈteɪ.bəl. ðeər ɪz ə ˈpeɪn.tɪŋ ɒn ðə wɔːl nɪər ðə ˈwɪn.dəʊ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember to link 'there is' smoothly as 'theriza' and 'there are' as 'therrar'. Stress the furniture words.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'There is' with singular nouns and 'There are' with plural nouns to describe a room. You should mention at least three different items and use both structures.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Look at the three story points below. Tell a short story about your bedroom. Use 'There is' and 'There are' to describe the furniture and things in it. Speak for about 30 seconds.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Now please describe your bedroom. What furniture is there? What things do you have on the walls or on the table? Use 'There is' and 'There are'.
storyPoints: Describe the main furniture in your bedroom (for example: a bed, a wardrobe, or a desk).
Talk about things on your desk or table (for example: books, a lamp, or a computer).
Mention something you like about your bedroom (for example: a comfortable bed, a nice window, or some photos).
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a comfortable bed and a big wardrobe in my bedroom. There are some books and a lamp on my desk. There is a nice window with curtains.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈkʌmf.tə.bəl bed ənd ə bɪɡ ˈwɔː.drəʊb ɪn maɪ ˈbed.ruːm. ðeər ɑːr sʌm bʊks ənd ə læmp ɒn maɪ desk. ðeər ɪz ə naɪs ˈwɪn.dəʊ wɪð ˈkɜː.tənz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'There is' before singular nouns like 'a bed' or 'a lamp'. Use 'There are' before plural nouns like 'books' or 'photos'. Speak slowly and clearly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task helps you practise describing a personal space. Using both 'There is' and 'There are' correctly shows you understand singular and plural structures. Adding adjectives like 'comfortable' or 'nice' makes your description more interesting.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are calling a friend to describe your new apartment. Your friend will ask you questions about the rooms and furniture. Answer using 'There is' and 'There are'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hi! I heard you moved to a new apartment! Tell me about it. What rooms are there?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You have just moved to a new apartment. Your friend is curious and calls you to ask about it. Describe the rooms and furniture in your new home. Use 'There is' for singular items and 'There are' for plural items.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a person who just moved to a new apartment. You are excited to tell your friend about your new home. Your apartment has a kitchen, a living room, a bedroom, and a bathroom.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There are four rooms in my new apartment. There is a small kitchen and a nice living room.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr fɔːr ruːmz ɪn maɪ njuː əˈpɑːt.mənt. ðeər ɪz ə smɔːl ˈkɪtʃ.ɪn ənd ə naɪs ˈlɪv.ɪŋ ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start by telling how many rooms there are, then describe each room. Use adjectives like 'small', 'big', or 'nice' before the nouns.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise a natural conversation about your home. Starting with the number of rooms and then giving details about each one is a good way to organise your description.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a furniture shop. The shop assistant asks what furniture you need for your bedroom. Tell them what you want using 'There is' and 'There are' to explain what you already have and what you need.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Welcome to our furniture shop! What furniture do you need for your bedroom? What do you already have?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are shopping for bedroom furniture. The shop assistant wants to help you. First, describe what furniture is already in your bedroom, then say what new furniture you need to buy.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a customer at a furniture shop. You already have a bed and a small table in your bedroom, but you need a new wardrobe and a bookshelf. Explain this to the shop assistant.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a bed and a small table in my bedroom. But there is no wardrobe. I need a wardrobe and a bookshelf.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə bed ənd ə smɔːl ˈteɪ.bəl ɪn maɪ ˈbed.ruːm. bʌt ðeər ɪz nəʊ ˈwɔː.drəʊb. aɪ niːd ə ˈwɔː.drəʊb ənd ə ˈbʊk.ʃelf/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'There is' to describe what you have. Use 'There is no...' to say what is missing. Then say 'I need...' for what you want to buy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises using 'There is' in both positive and negative forms. 'There is no wardrobe' is the negative form. This is a useful pattern for real-life shopping situations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are a hotel receptionist. A guest calls to ask about the hotel room. Describe what is in the room using 'There is' and 'There are'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hello, I have a reservation at your hotel. Can you tell me what is in the room, please?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A guest is calling the hotel to ask about their room before they arrive. As the receptionist, you need to describe the furniture and items in the hotel room clearly and politely.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a hotel receptionist. The hotel room has a double bed, a desk, a chair, a TV, a bathroom with a shower, and two towels. Describe the room to the guest politely.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a double bed and a desk with a chair. There is a TV on the wall. There are two towels in the bathroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈdʌb.əl bed ənd ə desk wɪð ə tʃeər. ðeər ɪz ə tiː viː ɒn ðə wɔːl. ðeər ɑːr tuː ˈtaʊ.əlz ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be polite and clear. List the items one by one. Use 'There is' for single items and 'There are' for two or more items.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay puts you in a professional situation. Describing a hotel room is a practical use of 'There is' and 'There are'. It also practises polite, clear communication.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are talking to your new roommate on the phone. Describe the shared kitchen and ask your roommate questions about what they want to bring.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hi! I'm your new roommate. Can you tell me about the kitchen? What is already there?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are moving into a shared flat. Your new roommate calls to ask about the kitchen. Describe what is already in the kitchen and ask if they have any items to bring.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You live in a shared flat. The kitchen already has a fridge, a table, and two chairs. There are some plates and cups in the cupboard. But there is no microwave. Ask your roommate if they have a microwave.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a fridge and a table in the kitchen. There are two chairs and some plates. There is no microwave. Do you have a microwave?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə frɪdʒ ənd ə ˈteɪ.bəl ɪn ðə ˈkɪtʃ.ɪn. ðeər ɑːr tuː tʃeəz ənd sʌm pleɪts. ðeər ɪz nəʊ ˈmaɪ.krə.weɪv. duː juː hæv ə ˈmaɪ.krə.weɪv/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe what is in the kitchen first, then mention what is missing. End with a question to your roommate using 'Do you have...?'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises describing a shared space. You use 'There is' and 'There are' for what exists, 'There is no' for what is missing, and a question form to interact with your roommate.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Focus on pronouncing the furniture and room vocabulary clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence clearly. Pay attention to the furniture words.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a wardrobe, a bookshelf, and a cupboard in the bedroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈwɔː.drəʊb, ə ˈbʊk.ʃelf, ənd ə ˈkʌb.əd ɪn ðə ˈbed.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be careful with 'cupboard' — it is pronounced 'KUB-ud', not 'cup-board'. 'Wardrobe' is 'WARD-rohb'. 'Bookshelf' is 'BOOK-shelf'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill focuses on furniture vocabulary that A1 learners often mispronounce. 'Cupboard' is especially tricky because the spelling does not match the pronunciation. Practise each word separately before saying the full sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentences out loud. Focus on using the correct form: 'There is' for singular and 'There are' for plural.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say these two sentences. Be careful to use 'There is' with one thing and 'There are' with more than one thing.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is one lamp on the table. There are four cushions on the sofa.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz wʌn læmp ɒn ðə ˈteɪ.bəl. ðeər ɑːr fɔːr ˈkʊʃ.ənz ɒn ðə ˈsəʊ.fə/
practicumQuestions.hint: Listen to the difference: 'There IS' uses /ɪz/ for one item. 'There ARE' uses /ɑːr/ for many items. Make sure you say the correct verb for each sentence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This grammar drill reinforces the core structure of the unit. The most common mistake is using 'There is' with plural nouns. By practising both forms in connected sentences, you build the habit of matching the verb to the noun.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay attention to which syllable is stressed in each underlined word: FURniture, BATHroom, COMfortable.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence. Stress the correct syllable in each long word. FURniture, BATHroom, COMfortable.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is comfortable furniture in the bathroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ˈkʌmf.tə.bəl ˈfɜː.nɪ.tʃər ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Stress the FIRST syllable in all three words: COMfortable (COM-fter-ble), FURniture (FUR-ni-cher), BATHroom (BATH-room). Do not stress the middle or last syllables.
practicumQuestions.explanation: English word stress follows patterns. Most two-syllable nouns and compound nouns stress the first syllable. 'Comfortable' is often reduced to three syllables in natural speech: COMF-ter-ble. Getting the stress right makes your English sound much more natural.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following two sentences out loud. The first is a yes/no question — use RISING intonation ↗. The second is a statement — use FALLING intonation ↘.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say both sentences. For the question, make your voice go UP at the end. For the statement, make your voice go DOWN at the end.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Is there a mirror in the bathroom? ↗ Yes, there is a mirror above the sink. ↘
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪz ðeər ə ˈmɪr.ər ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm ↗ jes, ðeər ɪz ə ˈmɪr.ər əˈbʌv ðə sɪŋk ↘/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the question 'Is there a mirror in the bathroom?', start at a normal pitch and let your voice RISE on 'bathroom?'. For the answer 'Yes, there is a mirror above the sink.', let your voice FALL on 'sink.'
practicumQuestions.explanation: Intonation is the music of English. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to signal that you are asking something. Statements use falling intonation to signal that you are giving information. Practising this pattern helps listeners understand whether you are asking or telling.

reading.question: According to the passage, what is on the floor in the living room?
reading.explanation: Maya writes 'There is also a soft rug on the floor' when she describes the living room. A rug is a small carpet that covers part of the floor.

reading.question: Which sentence from the passage uses 'There are' correctly?
options: There are four chairs around the table.
There are a new fridge in the kitchen.
There are a comfortable bed in my bedroom.
reading.answer: There are four chairs around the table.
reading.explanation: 'There are four chairs' is correct because 'four chairs' is plural (more than one). The other options have singular nouns ('a fridge', 'a bed'), so they need 'There is'.

reading.question: Maya says 'There isn't a dishwasher.' What does this mean?
options: The kitchen does not have a dishwasher.
The kitchen has a new dishwasher.
Maya wants to remove the dishwasher.
reading.answer: The kitchen does not have a dishwasher.
reading.explanation: 'There isn't' means 'there is not.' It tells us that something does NOT exist in that place. So the kitchen does not have a dishwasher.

reading.question: How many chairs are there in the kitchen?
reading.explanation: The passage says 'There are four chairs around the table' in the kitchen section. Always scan for numbers to find specific details!

reading.question: Choose the correct sentence about Maya's bathroom.
options: There is a mirror on the wall.
There are many plants in the bathroom.
There is a bookshelf in the bathroom.
reading.answer: There is a mirror on the wall.
reading.explanation: Maya says 'There is a mirror on the wall, but there aren't any plants yet.' So there IS a mirror, but there are NO plants. The bookshelf is in the bedroom, not the bathroom.

reading.question: Fill in the blank with the correct form: '_____ two bedrooms upstairs.'
reading.explanation: 'Two bedrooms' is plural (more than one), so we must use 'There are.' Remember: singular = 'There is', plural = 'There are'.

reading.question: What does Maya ask Lina to do at the end of the message?
options: Come and visit her new house.
Send her some money for plants.
reading.answer: Come and visit her new house.
reading.explanation: At the end, Maya writes 'Please come and visit me. You will love it!' She is inviting Lina to see her new home.

reading.question: Which room has a wardrobe?
reading.explanation: In the bedroom paragraph, Maya says 'there is a large wardrobe.' A wardrobe is a piece of furniture for keeping clothes, and it is commonly found in bedrooms.

reading.question: What is Jamie's nationality?
reading.explanation: Jamie is from Spain, so his nationality is Spanish.

reading.question: Which sentence is the correct negative form of 'She likes coffee'?
reading.explanation: For third person singular (she/he/it), we use 'doesn't + base verb'.

reading.question: Where do they usually eat dinner on weekdays?
reading.explanation: Daily routines typically describe having dinner at home with family.

reading.question: What time does the train to London depart?
reading.explanation: Standard timetable questions provide specific morning departure times.

reading.question: Choose the correct past form: 'Yesterday, we _____ a new car.'
reading.explanation: 'Buy' is an irregular verb whose past simple form is 'bought'.

reading.question: What does Maria do every Saturday morning?
reading.explanation: A routine action in the simple present tense describing Saturday morning.

reading.question: Which question is grammatically correct?
reading.explanation: Standard question order: Question Word + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you) + Verb (live).

writing.prompt: Write 3 sentences about your bedroom. Use 'There is' in one sentence and 'There are' in another sentence. Include one negative sentence with 'There isn't' or 'There aren't'.
writing.criteria: The answer must contain at least 3 complete sentences. One sentence uses 'There is' correctly with a singular noun. One sentence uses 'There are' correctly with a plural noun. One sentence is negative using 'There isn't' or 'There aren't'. All sentences must start with a capital letter and end with a period. Spelling of common furniture words must be correct.
writing.sampleGoodAnswer: There is a small bed in my bedroom. There are two pillows on the bed. There aren't any pictures on the wall.

writing.prompt: Look at this list of items: 1 fridge, 3 chairs, 1 table, 0 plants. Write 4 sentences about a kitchen using 'There is', 'There are', and 'There aren't' with these items.
writing.criteria: The answer must have 4 sentences. 'There is' must be used with singular items (fridge, table). 'There are' must be used with plural items (chairs). 'There aren't' must be used for items with zero quantity (plants with 'any'). Each sentence must have correct capitalization and punctuation. The noun after 'There are' must be plural.
writing.sampleGoodAnswer: There is a fridge in the kitchen. There are three chairs near the table. There is a table in the middle of the kitchen. There aren't any plants in the kitchen.

writing.prompt: Your friend wants to visit your house. Write a short message (at least 5 sentences) to describe your house. Tell your friend about the rooms and the furniture. Use 'There is', 'There are', 'There isn't', and 'There aren't'. You can also use one question with 'Is there' or 'Are there'.
writing.criteria: The answer must contain at least 5 complete sentences. It must use 'There is' at least once with a singular noun. It must use 'There are' at least once with a plural noun. It must include at least one negative form ('There isn't' or 'There aren't'). All sentences must have correct capitalization and end punctuation. Mention something on the wall or near the window (for example: a clock, a painting, or curtains).
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a big sofa in my living room. There are two small chairs and a coffee table. There is a painting on the wall near the window.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə bɪɡ ˈsəʊ.fə ɪn maɪ ˈlɪv.ɪŋ ruːm. ðeər ɑːr tuː smɔːl tʃeəz ənd ə ˈkɒf.i ˈteɪ.bəl. ðeər ɪz ə ˈpeɪn.tɪŋ ɒn ðə wɔːl nɪər ðə ˈwɪn.dəʊ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember to link 'there is' smoothly as 'theriza' and 'there are' as 'therrar'. Stress the furniture words.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'There is' with singular nouns and 'There are' with plural nouns to describe a room. You should mention at least three different items and use both structures.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Look at the three story points below. Tell a short story about your bedroom. Use 'There is' and 'There are' to describe the furniture and things in it. Speak for about 30 seconds.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Now please describe your bedroom. What furniture is there? What things do you have on the walls or on the table? Use 'There is' and 'There are'.
storyPoints: Describe the main furniture in your bedroom (for example: a bed, a wardrobe, or a desk).
Talk about things on your desk or table (for example: books, a lamp, or a computer).
Mention something you like about your bedroom (for example: a comfortable bed, a nice window, or some photos).
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a comfortable bed and a big wardrobe in my bedroom. There are some books and a lamp on my desk. There is a nice window with curtains.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈkʌmf.tə.bəl bed ənd ə bɪɡ ˈwɔː.drəʊb ɪn maɪ ˈbed.ruːm. ðeər ɑːr sʌm bʊks ənd ə læmp ɒn maɪ desk. ðeər ɪz ə naɪs ˈwɪn.dəʊ wɪð ˈkɜː.tənz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'There is' before singular nouns like 'a bed' or 'a lamp'. Use 'There are' before plural nouns like 'books' or 'photos'. Speak slowly and clearly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task helps you practise describing a personal space. Using both 'There is' and 'There are' correctly shows you understand singular and plural structures. Adding adjectives like 'comfortable' or 'nice' makes your description more interesting.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are calling a friend to describe your new apartment. Your friend will ask you questions about the rooms and furniture. Answer using 'There is' and 'There are'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hi! I heard you moved to a new apartment! Tell me about it. What rooms are there?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You have just moved to a new apartment. Your friend is curious and calls you to ask about it. Describe the rooms and furniture in your new home. Use 'There is' for singular items and 'There are' for plural items.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a person who just moved to a new apartment. You are excited to tell your friend about your new home. Your apartment has a kitchen, a living room, a bedroom, and a bathroom.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There are four rooms in my new apartment. There is a small kitchen and a nice living room.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr fɔːr ruːmz ɪn maɪ njuː əˈpɑːt.mənt. ðeər ɪz ə smɔːl ˈkɪtʃ.ɪn ənd ə naɪs ˈlɪv.ɪŋ ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start by telling how many rooms there are, then describe each room. Use adjectives like 'small', 'big', or 'nice' before the nouns.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise a natural conversation about your home. Starting with the number of rooms and then giving details about each one is a good way to organise your description.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a furniture shop. The shop assistant asks what furniture you need for your bedroom. Tell them what you want using 'There is' and 'There are' to explain what you already have and what you need.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Welcome to our furniture shop! What furniture do you need for your bedroom? What do you already have?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are shopping for bedroom furniture. The shop assistant wants to help you. First, describe what furniture is already in your bedroom, then say what new furniture you need to buy.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a customer at a furniture shop. You already have a bed and a small table in your bedroom, but you need a new wardrobe and a bookshelf. Explain this to the shop assistant.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a bed and a small table in my bedroom. But there is no wardrobe. I need a wardrobe and a bookshelf.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə bed ənd ə smɔːl ˈteɪ.bəl ɪn maɪ ˈbed.ruːm. bʌt ðeər ɪz nəʊ ˈwɔː.drəʊb. aɪ niːd ə ˈwɔː.drəʊb ənd ə ˈbʊk.ʃelf/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'There is' to describe what you have. Use 'There is no...' to say what is missing. Then say 'I need...' for what you want to buy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises using 'There is' in both positive and negative forms. 'There is no wardrobe' is the negative form. This is a useful pattern for real-life shopping situations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are a hotel receptionist. A guest calls to ask about the hotel room. Describe what is in the room using 'There is' and 'There are'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hello, I have a reservation at your hotel. Can you tell me what is in the room, please?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A guest is calling the hotel to ask about their room before they arrive. As the receptionist, you need to describe the furniture and items in the hotel room clearly and politely.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a hotel receptionist. The hotel room has a double bed, a desk, a chair, a TV, a bathroom with a shower, and two towels. Describe the room to the guest politely.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a double bed and a desk with a chair. There is a TV on the wall. There are two towels in the bathroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈdʌb.əl bed ənd ə desk wɪð ə tʃeər. ðeər ɪz ə tiː viː ɒn ðə wɔːl. ðeər ɑːr tuː ˈtaʊ.əlz ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be polite and clear. List the items one by one. Use 'There is' for single items and 'There are' for two or more items.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay puts you in a professional situation. Describing a hotel room is a practical use of 'There is' and 'There are'. It also practises polite, clear communication.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are talking to your new roommate on the phone. Describe the shared kitchen and ask your roommate questions about what they want to bring.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hi! I'm your new roommate. Can you tell me about the kitchen? What is already there?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are moving into a shared flat. Your new roommate calls to ask about the kitchen. Describe what is already in the kitchen and ask if they have any items to bring.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You live in a shared flat. The kitchen already has a fridge, a table, and two chairs. There are some plates and cups in the cupboard. But there is no microwave. Ask your roommate if they have a microwave.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a fridge and a table in the kitchen. There are two chairs and some plates. There is no microwave. Do you have a microwave?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə frɪdʒ ənd ə ˈteɪ.bəl ɪn ðə ˈkɪtʃ.ɪn. ðeər ɑːr tuː tʃeəz ənd sʌm pleɪts. ðeər ɪz nəʊ ˈmaɪ.krə.weɪv. duː juː hæv ə ˈmaɪ.krə.weɪv/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe what is in the kitchen first, then mention what is missing. End with a question to your roommate using 'Do you have...?'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises describing a shared space. You use 'There is' and 'There are' for what exists, 'There is no' for what is missing, and a question form to interact with your roommate.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Focus on pronouncing the furniture and room vocabulary clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence clearly. Pay attention to the furniture words.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is a wardrobe, a bookshelf, and a cupboard in the bedroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə ˈwɔː.drəʊb, ə ˈbʊk.ʃelf, ənd ə ˈkʌb.əd ɪn ðə ˈbed.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be careful with 'cupboard' — it is pronounced 'KUB-ud', not 'cup-board'. 'Wardrobe' is 'WARD-rohb'. 'Bookshelf' is 'BOOK-shelf'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill focuses on furniture vocabulary that A1 learners often mispronounce. 'Cupboard' is especially tricky because the spelling does not match the pronunciation. Practise each word separately before saying the full sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentences out loud. Focus on using the correct form: 'There is' for singular and 'There are' for plural.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say these two sentences. Be careful to use 'There is' with one thing and 'There are' with more than one thing.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is one lamp on the table. There are four cushions on the sofa.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz wʌn læmp ɒn ðə ˈteɪ.bəl. ðeər ɑːr fɔːr ˈkʊʃ.ənz ɒn ðə ˈsəʊ.fə/
practicumQuestions.hint: Listen to the difference: 'There IS' uses /ɪz/ for one item. 'There ARE' uses /ɑːr/ for many items. Make sure you say the correct verb for each sentence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This grammar drill reinforces the core structure of the unit. The most common mistake is using 'There is' with plural nouns. By practising both forms in connected sentences, you build the habit of matching the verb to the noun.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay attention to which syllable is stressed in each underlined word: FURniture, BATHroom, COMfortable.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence. Stress the correct syllable in each long word. FURniture, BATHroom, COMfortable.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: There is comfortable furniture in the bathroom.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ˈkʌmf.tə.bəl ˈfɜː.nɪ.tʃər ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Stress the FIRST syllable in all three words: COMfortable (COM-fter-ble), FURniture (FUR-ni-cher), BATHroom (BATH-room). Do not stress the middle or last syllables.
practicumQuestions.explanation: English word stress follows patterns. Most two-syllable nouns and compound nouns stress the first syllable. 'Comfortable' is often reduced to three syllables in natural speech: COMF-ter-ble. Getting the stress right makes your English sound much more natural.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following two sentences out loud. The first is a yes/no question — use RISING intonation ↗. The second is a statement — use FALLING intonation ↘.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say both sentences. For the question, make your voice go UP at the end. For the statement, make your voice go DOWN at the end.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Is there a mirror in the bathroom? ↗ Yes, there is a mirror above the sink. ↘
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪz ðeər ə ˈmɪr.ər ɪn ðə ˈbɑːθ.ruːm ↗ jes, ðeər ɪz ə ˈmɪr.ər əˈbʌv ðə sɪŋk ↘/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the question 'Is there a mirror in the bathroom?', start at a normal pitch and let your voice RISE on 'bathroom?'. For the answer 'Yes, there is a mirror above the sink.', let your voice FALL on 'sink.'
practicumQuestions.explanation: Intonation is the music of English. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to signal that you are asking something. Statements use falling intonation to signal that you are giving information. Practising this pattern helps listeners understand whether you are asking or telling.
